q: Our verifier wants calibration certificates for our meters. Which ones matter?
title: Meter calibration for verification
short: The meters whose readings become emissions: your own fuel flow meters, sub-meters, steam meters and the weighbridge. Utility meters belong to the discom or gas company, so their bill is the evidence. In India a weighbridge used for trade should carry a valid Legal Metrology stamp.

ul: Calibration reports for fuel flow meters and sub-meters.
Steam meter calibration, if used to allocate emissions.

sections.h: If a meter is out of date
p: Say so, use the reading with a note, and cross-check against invoices. Get it calibrated before the next period.
Discom and gas company meters are checked by them. Keep the bills; a verifier will not ask for their certificates.

senseible: Senseible keeps every figure linked to its source invoice or bill with a fingerprint, so a verifier can trace a total back to the documents it came from.
